acceptedScope.world: Busan railway station and KTX operational area only; freely traversable bounded site, not the Nampo/North Port city.
acceptedScope.experience: Single-player first person, Korean UI. PUBG/SuddenAttack/battle-royale references concern embodied movement, immediate interaction, readable spatial objectives and responsive feedback.
acceptedScope.player: KORAIL station staff: report, communicate/broadcast, guide passengers, control access and cooperate with NPC colleagues/responders.
acceptedScope.learning: Recall procedures through actions, consequences, NPC behaviour and radio acknowledgements. Ordinary mission completion feedback is sufficient.
acceptedScope.events: Authored terror/disaster missions. No scenario-draft generation. First increment is one fire-related evacuation mission.
constraints: No armed counterterror role, shooting or suspect-neutralization loop inferred from FPS references.
Root owns integration and native Unity validation; Astra low implements bounded lanes; no computer-use automation.
Jev may classify short inputs or support internal calculations with deterministic fallback; no public probabilities/forecast panel or generative mission authority.
Reuse installed Input System 1.20.0 and URP 17.3.0 from Packages/manifest.json; no dependency migration required for first slice.

firstMission.titleKo: 출입구 주변 연기 — 승객을 안전한 곳으로 안내
firstMission.purpose: One coherent station-staff evacuation response implemented as an authored playable fixture; not a scenario generator or verified current KORAIL manual training product.
firstMission.location: Source-existing exterior entrance apron/forecourt. Incident, staff, passengers, alternate route and meeting point all remain outside unsupported interior decks.
firstMission.bindingStatus: UNBOUND: choose actual supported native polygons and record their transforms/collider IDs; do not copy old ExitAnchor or ConcourseAnchor coordinates.

cast.countBoundary: Small authored gameplay population; no claim about real station occupancy.

authoredBoundary: Radio contact, PA request and colleague authority are provisional role-play affordances until exact KORAIL procedures are sourced.
Meeting point and blocked route are authored mission objects, never labelled as official evacuation geography.
Visible smoke may be a clearly scoped gameplay cue. It cannot imply calibrated spread, safe exposure, injuries or extinguishment.
Completion means the specified group reached the authored collection area and information was handed over; not that the fire is suppressed or the real station is safe.
learningInPlay: A nearby passenger reacts to the first warning and points out someone who has not moved.
Radio acknowledgement repeats the player-selected location and observation; missing information prompts correction within the conversation.
Colleague visibly walks to and holds the assigned approach; passengers do not comply until the action is acknowledged.
A passenger who misses the direction remains in the world until addressed; a returning passenger creates an access-control decision.
Responder asks about remaining people/last known position during the handoff; no later quiz or review screen.

stateNodes.name: On duty
stateNodes.entry: Spawn on validated ground; player has control; colleague and passengers are already present.
stateNodes.exitEvent: Player reaches a line-of-sight trigger for the incident cue.

stateNodes.name: Recognize and act
stateNodes.objectiveKo: 주변에 알리고 안전한 곳에서 상황을 전하세요.
actions: Report position/visible condition/people needing help to radio contact
stateNodes.order: Warning, movement and reporting can interleave. No requirement to approach the hazard or finish a phone UI before moving.

stateNodes.name: Coordinate
actions: Request the provisional broadcast via radio
Ask colleague to hold the unsafe approach
stateNodes.effects: Explicit acknowledgements change NPC assignments and objective facts; button acceptance alone does not move people.

stateNodes.name: Guide passengers
actions: Walk the valid route and address the group
Use the verified alternate path when the short path is blocked
stateNodes.effects: Each same passenger travels physically; behind-wall prompts, teleport completion and unsupported floor links are rejected.

stateNodes.name: Maintain control and account
actions: Account for the six identifiable passengers
Ask colleague to continue holding the approach
Prevent the scripted returning passenger from re-entering the incident zone through dialogue/guidance
stateNodes.effects: Accounting uses actual NPC state; movement and control continue while the radio is used.

stateNodes.name: Handoff
actions: Report incident location, observed condition and accounted/missing people
stateNodes.effects: No simulated treatment, fire suppression or reopening is inferred.

stateNodes.name: Mission clear
stateNodes.ui: Brief Korean in-world/radio completion acknowledgement plus ordinary restart/continue control.

stateNodes.name: Recoverable correction
stateNodes.effect: NPC/radio feedback identifies the immediate issue; player can correct within the same incident.

stateNodes.name: Technical blocked state
triggers: NPC stuck beyond declared recovery threshold
Missing authority required by a release claim
stateNodes.effect: Do not label a technical limitation as player procedural failure or successful training.

stateEdges.return: resume current stage after acknowledged correction
retry only after valid reset; never auto-clear

invariants: Warn/guide actions remain possible before a report is completed; assistance must not be artificially withheld by a linear checklist.
Player and NPC movement use the same validated geometric route; all goals use actual positions.
Repeated interaction cannot duplicate reports, spawn extra NPCs or advance a completed step twice.
No weapon mechanics or operations outside the station-staff role.
The mission graph is internal development state; no public graph or probability display.
authoredVariants: Short approach blocked, alternate exterior route open
Passenger missed instruction/tries to return, requiring renewed guidance
firstMission.duration: Aim for 5–8 minutes of active play for this first slice; pacing target only, never success from elapsed time.

firstNativeIncrement.scope: Playable first-person exterior traversal and one colleague interaction in the active official station world; no dependency on manual role-chain decisions.
implementation: Add a dedicated FPS runtime root and camera/controller using installed Input System; disable competing RTS input/camera/HUD only in FPS mode.
Bind a grounded spawn and short exterior loop only after downward support rays plus capsule overlap/sweep checks.
Use metre dimensions, CharacterController or equivalent collision-aware locomotion, yaw/pitch, gravity, cursor capture/release and a contextual interaction ray.
Place one colleague target on verified ground; Korean E prompt and acknowledged line respond only inside reach and line of sight.
Exit/return to play resets input safely; preserve raw source assets and archived RTS systems.
acceptance: Native Unity Play Mode: actual Input System Move/Look/Interact events traverse the loop and reach the colleague.
No fall-through, wall penetration, roof spawn or movement over unsupported interior on that route.
Pause/focus loss releases cursor and suppresses movement; resume has no stuck keys or duplicate input.
World and Korean interaction text are readable in fresh correctly sized game frames.
Record exact scene/script/input hashes, anchor/collider manifest, route trace and screenshots in a root-owned receipt.
firstNativeIncrement.completionLabel: FPS locomotion/interaction increment PASS only; not first-mission completion and not product A.

priorityFiles.action: Root-owned integration: explicit FPS mode/root; only one active controlling camera/input path.
Proposed dedicated controller/interactor/mission/NPC/HUD modules; exact filenames may follow the ongoing locomotion owner. Do not duplicate that lane.
Inspect bindings and context ownership; add isolated FPS actions or a dedicated FPS action asset without both maps consuming play input.
Reuse focus/modal ownership contract where compatible; verify cursor and FPS look suppression with UI open.
Reuse published source and rigid registration; do not rebuild/squash official meshes to fit old floor anchors.
Archive/disable RTS camera and management HUD in FPS mode; preserve unrelated backend state and old receipts.
Inspect reusable contracts; replace old floor-bound mission routing. Keep old FDS/crowd reference data out of unverified new site predictions.
Retain only relevant internal bounded classification/calculation; forecast UI stays outside FPS player experience.
Root updates canonical direction and scorecard once it adopts scope/rubric. This planning worker must not edit them.

evidenceGates.adoption: Root must record adoption and freeze before evaluating. Scope change is explicit; no retroactive PASS from old receipts and no averaging missing domains.
evidenceGates.productVsSlice: FPS-I0 and FPS-M01 are increments. Product A evaluates the accepted station/KTX FPS scope, including source-grounded terror and disaster mission coverage; an exterior fire slice cannot substitute for it.

domains.name: Playable first-person mission loop
domains.pass: Native single-player play physically connects recognition, reporting/communication, NPC cooperation, passenger guidance, site control and handoff. The accepted release mission set includes at least one disaster and one terror-related staff response with source-matched duties. Normal, route-blocked and delayed/missed-communication variants remain playable and correctable. Completion follows world/NPC state, not button sequence or waiting. No separate debrief/quiz is required.

domains.name: FPS reference application and role fit
domains.pass: A source-to-runtime comparison maps movement/look responsiveness, interaction reach/visibility, spatial objectives, audiovisual acknowledgement and tension from the selected FPS references to station-staff play. Independent native review confirms actual embodied choices and readable consequences. No score for copied combat, resource building or shooter art alone.

domains.name: First-person usability and Korean presentation
domains.pass: Test real Input System handlers for movement/look/interact, invalid/out-of-range/occluded targets, cancel, radio/menu focus, pause, cursor release and re-entry. At declared supported resolutions Korean prompts remain legible without blocking hazards/passengers; objectives can be followed without internal implementation knowledge. Fresh game captures and input traces required; no OS/human-parity inference.

domains.name: Station/KTX geometry and character presentation
domains.pass: Every release mission route, including the accepted KTX access/play area, has continuous collision, grounded spawn, correct door/platform/step scale and NPC navigation. Source-existing versus authored geometry is recorded. Close first-person views have coherent material scale, legible roles and walk/wait/guide/hold behaviour; no core placeholder route or inaccessible hollow interior passed as complete.

domains.name: Bounded open site and performance
domains.pass: Station/KTX playable boundary and all release routes are traversable with blocked-route recovery; outside-city travel is excluded. On declared hardware/resolution, player-build warm and sustained mission runs including crowded turns have p95 frame time <=33.3 ms, no crashes/stalls/unbounded memory growth, and correctly timed captures.

domains.name: Deterministic mission and durable state
domains.pass: Typed accepted events advance mission/NPC state once. Pause/retry/focus loss, duplicate/stale acknowledgements and fallback responses preserve invariants. Save/reload or checkpoint restart restores player, passengers, incident flags and assignments consistently. Late Jev replies cannot revise completed actions. No evacuation-as-medical-recovery or timer-as-extinguishment.

domains.name: Computational verification and validation
domains.pass: Retain the existing scientific evidence boundary: all claimed fire/smoke/crowd/contact/health outcomes require applicable pinned published V&V, units/time/coupling/convergence and source-supported tolerances. The short old reference field cannot be stretched across the new geometry or mission time. A procedural cue-only slice has no predictive-physics PASS.

domains.name: Procedure and real-site authority
domains.pass: Every release-critical staff action is mapped to a dated applicable public manual or operator-confirmed procedure; match incident, role and site scope. Geometry/exits/occupancy/material/ventilation used in site-outcome claims retain provenance and uncertainty, with independent observed site validation for those claims. General guidance or an old different-incident chart cannot certify Busan procedures or as-built outcomes.
